selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What mistake does the nafs make about life that leads to boredom with worship?
questions.answer: It acts as if life will keep going for a long time and forgets that death may come soon.

questions.question: According to the passage, how much time out of a full day is being discussed for this act of worship?
questions.answer: One hour out of twenty-four.

questions.question: How is that act of worship described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as good, easy, gentle, and full of mercy.

questions.question: What greater benefit comes from spending that hour in worship?
questions.answer: It helps a person gain the real joy of the everlasting life.

questions.question: If a person truly understood how short life is, how would that change his attitude toward worship?
questions.answer: He would not feel annoyed by it. He would feel eager and pleased to do it.

questions.question: What does the passage say is happening to a person’s life besides being short?
questions.answer: It is passing away and being wasted.

questions.question: What idea about this world is being corrected in the warning?
questions.answer: The false idea that a person is here to keep enjoying worldly life for a very long time.

questions.question: What false attitude toward worldly enjoyment is criticized?
questions.answer: Living as if this world is the place of endless pleasure.

questions.question: In the First Warning, what question is used to challenge the nafs about its future?
questions.answer: It is asked whether it has any sure proof that it will even reach tomorrow or next year.

questions.question: Why does the nafs become tired of worship, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because it imagines that it will live forever.

questions.question: What truth about human life is emphasized in this warning?
questions.answer: Human life is short and uncertain.

questions.question: What is wrong with delaying worship as if there will always be more time later?
questions.answer: It ignores that life may end soon and wastes a valuable chance to prepare for the Hereafter.

questions.question: What does the warning teach about using time wisely?
questions.answer: Even a small part of the day should be used for worship because it brings a huge and lasting reward.

questions.question: What kind of happiness is connected to this worship?
questions.answer: Lasting happiness in eternal life.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the time spent in worship to the whole day?
questions.answer: It shows that the time is very small compared with the full day.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the value of time from this warning?
questions.answer: Time is precious and should not be wasted because life passes quickly.

questions.question: Who is being addressed in the First Warning?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own nafs, meaning the lower self.

questions.question: What does the warning suggest about being certain of tomorrow?
questions.answer: A person cannot be certain of it at all.

questions.question: What two facts should remove that complaint?
questions.answer: Life is short, and the time used for worship is small but very rewarding.

questions.question: Why is the act of worship called merciful in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it is a kindness from Allah that leads a person toward true and lasting success.

questions.question: What happens when life passes without good use?
questions.answer: It goes away in a wasted way.

questions.question: How does this warning connect dunya and akhirah?
questions.answer: It teaches that a little effort in this world can lead to real happiness in the next life.

questions.question: Is the warning presenting worship as harmful, neutral, or beneficial? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: Beneficial, because it is easy, beautiful, and leads to eternal good.

questions.question: What is one cause-and-effect link in the passage?
questions.answer: Thinking you will live forever leads to boredom with worship.
